question: BS Yediyurappa resigned as the Chief Minister of Karnataka for the ________________ time in July 2021.
solution:
The correct answer is __**fourth.**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• After days of speculation, Yediyurappa resigned as Chief Minister on 26 July 2021, the second anniversary of his fourth term. He was succeeded by his Protege, Basavaraj Bommai, on 28 July 2021.
 
• Bookanakere Siddalingappa Yediyurappa **often referred to by his initials **BSY**, is an** Indian politician** who served as the **19th chief** **minister of karnataka** and currently a Member of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly. 
 
• He is a member of the **Bharatiya Janta Party**. He is also the only politician so far in Karnataka to have served four times as Chief Minister and three times as **Leader of the opposition** in the **karnataka legislative assembly .**
 
• In 1965, he was appointed a first-division clerk in the social welfare department but he quit the job and moved on to **Shikaripura**** **where he joined as a clerk at Veerabhadra Shastri's Shankara rice mill.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In 2011, he resigned after being indicted over a corruption case; he was acquitted in 2016.Owing to alleged ill-treatment meted out to Yediyurappa by the BJP High Command, he left BJP and formed his own party, the** ****Karnataka Janata Paksha**
 
• On 17 May 2018, he was sworn in as the chief minister, his third term in the office .Unable to get majority support in the Assembly, he resigned just two days after taking office, after which **H.D Kumaraswamy** took oath as the chief minister.
 
• After the government of **kumaraswamy** lost its majority in July 2019 with the resignation of 17 MLAs, Yediyurappa took oath as the chief minister and proved his majority. In the December by-elections, BJP won 12 seats out of 15 and gained a majority of 117 seats under his leadership, cementing his win.
